brief: Weekly GS Prime/Shares/Derivatives rundown. The S&P 500 fell 0.5%; US equities were net sold a 3rd straight week, the largest single-stock de-grossing since late July, concentrated in Industrials (fastest HF selling pace in 6+ months), while Staples and Real Estate were bought hardest, signaling a defensive posture. Net TMT selling over the past two weeks (~$20bn) is approaching July's AI-selloff pace (~$23bn), with little rotation into defensives this time. Thursday brought a capitulation/de-grossing episode on AI financing worries plus Iran/Israel/US military escalation, driving the GS Risk Appetite Indicator to its lowest since April and the NDX-SPX implied-vol spread to a 98th-percentile 5-year high. GS calls this an HF deleveraging episode where short-term stops dominate over medium-term value, and recommends buying the AI dip selectively (Power, Hyperscalers, Inference, Cyber) via a GSTMTAIP call spread, funded by shorting cyclicals (GSXUCYCL puts) given slowing growth and tighter financial conditions. Separately, Managed Money kept adding Brent long calls (~$1bn through Oct 20) on Gulf shipping disruption even as put-call skew cheapened. Earnings produced wide single-name dispersion across Industrials, Materials and Healthcare. Next week brings FOMC/BOC/ECB/BOJ decisions, 44% of S&P market cap reporting, and Brazil's election (Polymarket: Bolsonaro 76%, despite tightening polls).
